A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRISP study. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model perplexity and multiple-choice accuracy experiments, including fine-tuning, scaling, clustering ablations and task-transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds downstream results using GTE embeddings and a cross-entropy-difference selection baseline.

M1.justification: CRISP retains the same clustering, specialist-histogram estimation and generalist-data sampling procedure. Algorithm 1 corrects the sampling set from Ds to Dg and the batch indexing, aligning the pseudocode with v1's existing explanation rather than establishing a changed method. GTE is an embedding ablation.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix B adds an auxiliary comparison using MTEB clustering-accuracy results. Redpj2, the three specialist language-modeling domains, ARC-E/C, MMLU and RWDB-R remain unchanged; the new GTE and CED downstream experiments use existing tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix I and Table 14 add cross-entropy difference (CED) to the 1.3B-model comparison on ARC-E, ARC-C and MMLU, alongside Base, DoGE, Classifier and CRISP. v1 discussed this approach in related work but did not report its evaluation.

E3.justification: New experiments use GTE-small embeddings across clustering resolutions and a CED selector based on a 350m-parameter generalist LM and its specialist fine-tuned counterpart. Existing dataset splits, model-training budgets, prompts and accuracy normalization remain unchanged; the additions do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B extends the SBERT-versus-LSI representation analysis with GTE-small and an embedding cost-versus-quality comparison. Table 3 tests how GTE's downstream benefit depends on cluster count. Existing repetition, data-size, scaling, transfer and continued-pretraining analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing quantile and shaded displays are retained, and the new tables do not introduce uncertainty reporting. Appendix I's word 'significantly' is not accompanied by a statistical test.

E6.justification: v2 adds embedding cost/accuracy entries, GTE results and CED accuracies. At 64 clusters, Table 3 reports ARC-E accuracy of 67.8 for GTE versus 65.2 for SBERT; Table 14 adds CED scores of 58.9/30.5/31.1 for ARC-E/C/MMLU. These are additional comparisons, not improved scores for an unchanged configuration. Retained results match, apart from correcting the repetition mean in Section 5.1 from 1.94 to 1.95, consistent with Figure 6.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the final importance-weighted expectation from sampling clusters under the specialist distribution to sampling under the generalist distribution. This repairs the importance-sampling identity. The conditional-independence assumptions and remaining mathematical development are retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that clustered importance sampling enables effective specialist LMs from scarce specialist data, with benefits across model sizes, multitasking and continued pretraining. v2 names CRISP and emphasizes novelty more explicitly in the abstract, but v1 already identifies scaled clustered importance sampling as its contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds an interpretation of embedding cost-quality tradeoffs and GTE's benefits at smaller cluster counts. Appendix I discusses CED's scoring expense, but incorrectly states that CED improves over the classifier: Table 14 places CED below it on all three tasks. Existing applicability and overfitting discussions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly reports embedding costs on H100 hardware, including 5.4k GPU hours for MiniLM-L6-v2 over Redpj2, and identifies alternative encoders. Appendix I documents CED's 350m-parameter selector, specialist fine-tuning and two scoring passes. Existing hyperparameter tables and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MTEB, E5 and GTE: Muennighoff et al. (2023b), Wang et al. (2022) and Li et al. (2023). It also evaluates previously discussed CED research. The broader positioning as a scalable extension of Grangier et al. (2024b) remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises parts of the abstract and conclusion, adds an introductory overview, makes localized language corrections and updates acknowledgments. Two appendix sections are inserted, while the main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2, 3 and 14; Table 3 also tabulates existing SBERT/LSI results from Figure 5. It revises Figure 1's caption, relocates Algorithm 1 and several displays, and adds conference headers. Existing figures and table designs are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency and reproducibility through the importance-sampling and pseudocode corrections, embedding-cost disclosure, and additional GTE and CED comparisons. These provide useful support without substantially changing the study. The new contradiction between Appendix I's CED interpretation and Table 14 reduces clarity, but the localized error does not outweigh the gains in correctness, transparency and comparative evidence.
